chunks: From him, from Hammad, from Shu'ayb, from Abi Basir, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

If a man sleeps and does not perform the Maghrib prayer and the later 'Isha' prayer, or he forgets, then if he awakens before dawn with enough time to perform both of them, let him perform them both. If he fears that one of them will escape him, then let him begin with the later 'Isha' prayer. And if he awakens after dawn, then let him begin by performing Fajr, then Maghrib, then the later 'Isha' before sunrise. But if he fears that the sun will rise and one of the two prayers will escape him, then let him perform Maghrib and leave the later 'Isha' until the sun rises and its rays go away, then let him perform it.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: What this report contains regarding delaying the makeup prayer until after sunrise is to be understood as taqiyyah, because it is the view of some of the 'ammah. What we act upon is what we stated earlier: that he makes up the obligatory prayer at whatever time it may be, by night or by day.

key_terms.التَّقِيَّةِ: dissimulation or precautionary conformity, used here in interpreting the report
key_terms.الْعِشَاءِ الْآخِرَةِ: the 'Isha' prayer, referred to here as the later night prayer
key_terms.الْفَجْرِ: the time of dawn, affecting the order of performance and makeup
key_terms.الْفَرْضَ: the obligatory prayer duty that must be made up
key_terms.الْقَضَاءِ: making up a missed obligatory prayer
key_terms.صَلَاةَ الْمَغْرِبِ: the Maghrib prayer missed by sleep or forgetfulness
key_terms.طُلُوعِ الشَّمْسِ: sunrise, a time marker relevant to the sequencing mentioned in the report

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on making up Maghrib and 'Isha' if someone slept through them or forgot them?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the ruling for one who missed Maghrib and 'Isha' due to sleep or forgetfulness, detailing the order in which the prayers should be made up depending on the time of awakening. The compiler then clarifies that the instruction to delay 'Isha' until after sunrise is interpreted as taqiyyah, while the operative ruling in Shia fiqh is that missed obligatory prayers may be made up at any time of night or day.
